notice: Sample leaflets written for this prototype: general information in plain words, not about any one patient and not medical advice. A real deployment shows the hospital's own approved patient leaflets instead.

leaflets.title: Moving about after hip surgery
sentences: After hip surgery, the physiotherapist decides when and how the patient gets up, and with which walking aid.
Use the walking aid you were given every time you walk, until the physiotherapist says otherwise.
If the care team has said to ask for help before getting out of bed, ask every time.
Feeling dizzy when standing up can happen after surgery: sit back down and tell the nurse or carer.
Do the exercises the physiotherapist showed you, as often as they said.
Ask the physiotherapist which movements to avoid while the hip heals.

leaflets.title: Preventing falls at home
sentences: Clear rugs, cables and clutter from the routes she uses most at home.
Leave a light on the way to the toilet at night.
Keep the things she uses every day within easy reach, so she does not need to bend or climb.
Wear shoes or slippers that fit well and have a back.
Ask the care team or the GP about a home safety check and equipment such as a raised toilet seat or grab rails.

leaflets.title: Blood-thinning injections at home
sentences: Some patients go home with daily injections that lower the risk of blood clots after hip surgery.
Give the injection at about the same time each day, the way the nurse or pharmacist showed you.
A small bruise where the needle went in can happen.
Do not stop the injections early unless the doctor says so.
Call the GP or the ward if there is bleeding that does not stop, blood in urine or stools, or large bruises.
Put used needles in the sharps bin you were given.

leaflets.title: Caring for the wound and staples
sentences: Keep the dressing clean and dry until the nurse says otherwise.
Staples are taken out by a nurse, at the GP practice or at home, on the date you were given.
Do not soak the wound in a bath until the care team says it has healed.
Call the GP or the ward if the wound becomes hot, red or swollen, leaks, or smells.

leaflets.title: Warning signs after hip surgery
sentences: Call your local emergency number if she has chest pain or sudden shortness of breath.
Call the GP or the ward the same day if the leg becomes hot, red, swollen or painful.
Call the GP or the ward if she has a fever or the wound leaks.
Call the GP or the ward if she cannot put weight on the leg when she could before, or the leg looks shorter or turned outwards.

leaflets.title: Pain relief after hip surgery
sentences: Take pain relief as written on the medication list, and not more than the list says.
Many cold and flu medicines also contain paracetamol: check the labels so it is not taken twice.
Tell the GP or the pharmacist if the pain is getting worse instead of better.
